answer: The anchor multiplier is published, charged in ferrous, and thread lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3532 identities would post 2374 proofs and burn roughly 60 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
